title: Scalar naturality of the canonical inner open-refinement map
statement: Let R,S and a:R→S be compatible pro-etale ring-sheaf coefficients [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data, def-sp-coefficient-mate-comparisons]. For compactifications c,d of f:X→Y, a refinement r:c→d [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and canonical open-triangle coefficient composition equalities hR,hS, let alphaR,alphaS be the canonical refinementOpenMap transformations [lem-sf-refinement-open-restriction]. For every unbounded derived R_X-module M, T_dZ(alphaR(M)) followed by properComparison(a,r) at j_c,! over R of M followed by Rr_* over S of openComparison(a,c.i) at M equals openComparison(a,d.i) at M followed by alphaS(T_X M). This is the inner forward refinement square, without an outer proper map, a proper compositor, inverse refinement arrows or a changed input vertex.

source.place: Tags 03DI, 0D6D and 07A6: inverse image, change of coefficients and adjunction mates; Zheng Section 5, 5.13--5.15.

proof.text: Extend the expression refinementRestriction to a natural transformation on all derived modules on c.Z, by the refinement pullback compositor followed by pullback of the proper counit. Its restriction to the image of j_c,! is the specified refinementRestriction.

Invert scalarPull_geometric_composition and eliminate the open triangle equality to get coherence for refinementPull. Use properComparison_mate_square and mateEquiv_counit to obtain the proper scalar counit equation. Naturality of refinementPull and scalarPull, together with this counit equation, proves coefficient naturality of the restriction transformation.

The generic coefficientOpen_unit gives the open scalar unit equation. OpenComparison is invertible, so append its inverse to obtain the inverse unit equation. At j_c,! of T_X M the restriction transformation is invertible by exists_refinementRestriction. Apply the generic coefficient_refinement_of_restriction: transpose under the S-open adjunction, postcompose with that invertible restriction, use its coefficient naturality, and the two refinementOpenMap normalizations. Cancel the restriction and use injectivity of the Hom equivalence.

proof_origin.note: Ordinary derived-category mate calculation, with no coefficient-system realization.

lean.statement:
theorem refinementOpenMap_scalar
    {R S : Coefficients.{u}} (a : Change R S)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (hR : R.pull (c.i ≫ r.hom) = proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients c.i r.hom
      (R.ring d.Z) (R.ring c.Z) (R.ring X) (R.pull r.hom) (R.pull c.i))
    (hS : S.pull (c.i ≫ r.hom) = proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients c.i r.hom
      (S.ring d.Z) (S.ring c.Z) (S.ring X) (S.pull r.hom) (S.pull c.i))
    (M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X))) :
    (pbcDerivedExtend (a.map d.Z)).map ((refinementOpenMap R r hR).app M) ≫
        (properComparison a r.hom).app ((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) ≫
        (push S r.hom).map ((openComparison a c.i).app M) =
      (openComparison a d.i).app M ≫
        (refinementOpenMap S r hS).app ((pbcDerivedExtend (a.map X)).obj M)
